newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bond yields simmering, pondering rates.
newsitem.headline: Australian bond yields simmering, pondering rates.

text.p: *Australian bonds continued to fluctuate in a narrow trading range as the market simmered down after Thursday's short-end sell-off and pondered next week's Reserve Bank board meeting.
Australian bond yields continued to fluctuate in a narrow trading range as the market simmered down after Thursday's short-end sell-off and pondered next week's Reserve Bank board meeting.

A report by an influential U.S. investment bank on Wednesday caused anxiety in the market, as while it still gave a 75 percent chance of an easing, it felt that the market had been too over-confident in it happening next week.
September bill futures have since pulled back to just fully price in a 25 basis points easing in current 5.5 official interest rates, rather than the full 50 basis points.

The board meeting is on July 1, and at the same time the Federal Open Market Committee meets on July 1 and 2, which the RBA will be taking into account when it makes its decision. Complicating the rate cut hopes will be the release of May retail trade on July 2, which are statistically expected to rebound after back to back negatives in March and April, but the extent of the recovery could also have a bearing on rate expectations, analysts said.
However, despite the market's hesitancy, it out-performed the U.S. market which succumbed to a late sell-off on Wednesday amid talk of central bank selling.

The U.S. sell-off came despite a successful U.S. five-year note auction. The Canadian market followed the U.S. trend and was also undermined by a weaker Canadian dollar. The New Zealand market slightly outperformed as it digested the N.Z. budget.
